sections.h2: Where is the Brown County Register of Deeds and when can you record a deed?
sections.html:
The Brown County Register of Deeds is in the Northern Building, Room 260, at 305 E. Walnut Street in Green Bay. The mailing address is P.O. Box 23600, Green Bay, WI 54305-3600, and the phone number is 920-448-4470.

The county's register page lists public hours of 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 to 11:30 a.m. on Friday. Walk-in real estate recordings stop earlier: 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 10:30 a.m. on Friday. Plan your drop-off around the earlier cutoff, and call to confirm the hours before a closing day.

The office records the deeds, land contracts, mortgages and plats for the whole county, and it also issues vital records. Under s. 59.43, it stamps each recorded document with the date, hour and minute and files them in the order received.

sections.h2: What is tag-less recording and the Swift Agreement in Brown County?
sections.html:
Brown County has moved to a tag-less recording system, and anyone sending paper documents for recording must also send a completed Swift Agreement. The agreement gives you access to the official copy after the document is recorded.

Once the deed is recorded, you get an email with a secure link. The link lets you print up to three copies and stays valid for seven days, so save the file the day it arrives. A seller who wants a permanent copy for the closing binder should download and store the PDF right away.

State law adds a mailing rule. A register must deliver recorded documents to the recipient named by the submitter once adequate postage is provided, unless the submitter has agreed to another arrangement (s. 59.43(1c)(g)). Name the recipient and give an email address on the Swift Agreement.

sections.h2: How do you search Brown County land records?
sections.html:
Land records searching, which the county calls Laredo, is available by advance appointment only. Call 920-448-4470 to book a time. Do not plan a same-day walk-in search the morning of a closing.

Copies of recorded documents carry a state-set price: $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page of a document, plus $1 to certify a copy (s. 59.43(2)(b)). Ask your title company whether it will run the search for the sale, and give it the parcel number from your tax bill.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Brown County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed, mortgage or similar document in Brown County costs $30, the flat rate in s. 59.43(2)(ag). The statute requires payment in advance.

  • $30 for a deed, mortgage, satisfaction or land contract.
  • $50 for a cemetery plat, subdivision plat or condominium plat.
  • $2 plus $1 per added page for a copy, and $1 more to certify it.
  • The state transfer fee, if the sale is not exempt, is paid by the seller on top of the recording fee.

Because the register collects the transfer fee when it takes the deed, budget for both amounts at the same counter visit or in the same e-recording batch.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer fee on a Brown County home sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays $3 for every $1,000 of value, or 30 cents per $100 or fraction of $100, under s. 77.22. On a house worth $266,000, the Census Bureau's median value for Brown County owner-occupied homes, the fee is $798.00.

The Department of Revenue's RETR overview tells filers to use the sale price, including any mortgage balance. For a gift or other transfer without a price, an unappraised property is reported at the estimated full value on the latest property tax bill. Personal property in the sale, such as appliances or furniture, goes on a separate line and is left out of the fee base.

Several points apply to Brown County deals in particular:

  • Parts of Howard and Wrightstown lie in Outagamie County. A transfer with parcels in two counties needs a separate return for each county.
  • A deed that completes a land contract owes no second fee if the proper fee was paid when the contract was recorded (s. 77.25(17)).
  • No city, village, town or county may charge a fee on a conveyance that is exempt from the state fee (s. 77.256).
  • Every grantor and grantee on the deed must be listed on the return individually.

The register hands each month's fees and returns to the county treasurer by the 15th, and the county keeps 20 percent (ss. 77.23 and 77.24).

sections.h2: What gets a deed rejected at the Brown County counter?
sections.html:
A deed gets rejected when it misses a format item in s. 59.43(2m) or carries a Social Security number. The register may also turn away a whole set of related documents if one fails. Check these points before you sign:

  • A blank 3 by 3 inch space in the upper right corner of page one.
  • The parcel identification number for each parcel affected.
  • Return information on the first page, unless the document is recorded electronically.
  • White paper, at least 20 pound, 8.5 inches wide and 11 or 14 inches long, with no hinged pages.
  • Legible black, blue or red ink and clearly printed grantor, grantee and notary names.
  • No Social Security number anywhere in the document.

The register is not required to judge value or exemptions, so those entries are the filers' responsibility. Intentionally falsifying a value on a return can bring a fine of up to $1,000, up to a year in the county jail, or both, according to the DOR overview.

sections.h2: What is Brown County like for people selling a house?
sections.html:
Brown County is the fourth most populous county in Wisconsin and part of the Green Bay metro area. It covers 616 square miles, of which 86 are water, and Interstates 41 and 43 and U.S. Highways 41 and 141 run through it. The county seat moved from Menomoneeville (now part of Allouez) to De Pere in 1837 and to Green Bay in 1854.

Green Bay and De Pere are the two cities. The villages are Allouez, Ashwaubenon, Bellevue, Denmark, Greenleaf, Hobart, Howard, Pulaski, Suamico and Wrightstown, with a ring of towns around them. School districts that serve the county include Green Bay Area, De Pere Unified, Ashwaubenon, Howard-Suamico, Pulaski Community, Denmark, Wrightstown Community and several others.

The deed is recorded at this one county office whichever town, village or city the house is in. Property tax is different: the county treasurer collects first-installment taxes for only some Brown County municipalities, so check your bill for the right payee.

faqs.q: What are the Brown County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The county page lists public hours of 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 to 11:30 a.m. Friday. Walk-in real estate recordings are taken until 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 10:30 a.m. Friday. Call 920-448-4470 to confirm before you go.

faqs.q: Do I need a Swift Agreement to record a deed in Brown County?
faqs.a: Yes, if you submit paper documents. The county moved to tag-less recording, and paper filers must include a completed Swift Agreement. It gives you access to the official copy, which arrives by emailed link for printing up to three copies within seven days.

faqs.q: How do I search Brown County land records?
faqs.a: Land records searching, called Laredo, is by advance appointment only. Call 920-448-4470 to schedule. Ask your title company whether it runs the search for you. The state sets copy prices at $2 for the first page of a copy and $1 for each added page.

faqs.q: How much is the real estate transfer fee in Brown County?
faqs.a: It is the same statewide: 30 cents per $100 of value, charged to the seller under s. 77.22. A $266,000 sale produces a $798.00 fee. Gifts between parent and child, transfers by will and foreclosure deeds to the mortgage holder are among the exemptions in s. 77.25.

faqs.q: Can the Brown County register record a deed that has a Social Security number?
faqs.a: No. Section 59.43(1m) bars a register of deeds from recording a document that contains an individual's Social Security number. Remove it before you submit the deed. The transfer return collects identifiers separately through the Department of Revenue.
